newsitem.title: USA: MCI bonds tighten after BT announcement.
newsitem.headline: MCI bonds tighten after BT announcement.

text.p: Bonds of MCI Communications Corp rallied substantially on speculation that a potential merger between the company and British Telecommunications Plc would cause rating agencies to upgrade MCI debt.
Frank Plumley, director at Standard & Poor's, said that market speculation may be correct.

"BT is rated triple-A and MCI is rated single-A. In the event of a merger, we would expect the gap to close. As to where it will shake out, that will depend on the terms of the deal and the source of funding," he said.
Plumley said S&P is likely to make a more formal announcement about the ratings implications of the potential merger on MCI and BT debt on Monday.
Calls to Moody's Investors Service were not immediately returned.
A trader said, "MCI senior debt has tightened six to seven basis points. The company has already been trading pretty tight for a single-A credit. Now it's trading closer to a double-A profile."
He noted both short- and long-term issues of MCI debt such as its 6.95 percent senior notes due '06 as well as its 7 3/4 percent senior notes due '24, had tightened by the same amount.
The trader said news of the potential merger of BT and MCI had not affected other investment-grade telecommunications credits such as AT&T Corp and Sprint Corp.
Shares of Sprint soared 12 percent late Friday, although AT&T's stock remained unchanged.

In the more volatile high-yield market, bonds in the telecommunications sector were up approximately 3/4 of a point across the board. UK cable junk bonds such as International Cabletel, Diamond Cable Ltd and TeleWest Plc were up a point, trader said.
Trader were perplexed by the gains, noting there was no direct connection between these companies and MCI and BT.

A telecommunications analyst noted, however, "The addition of a very real buyer on the radar screen implicitly makes people take a second look at valuations. There's bound to be some movement among high-yield telecommunications credits. The implications are positive because this is an increasingly global business."
